newsitem.title: Germany: SOCCER-BAYERN RALLY FOR GERMAN CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN RALLY FOR GERMAN CUP WIN.

text.p: Bayern Munich rallied from an early 1-0 deficit to defeat Borussia Moenchengladbach 2-1 away and advance to the third round of the German Cup on Wednesday night.
Rebounding from a stinging 3-0 defeat by Werder Bremen in a Bundesliga match on Saturday and their early exit from the UEFA Cup last week, Bayern pulled off a badly needed victory.
"This was a very important win for us," said Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni, who has come under pressure after his side's recent lacklustre performances. "Both teams could have won tonight."
Moenchengladbach, who clearly outplayed the visitors in the opening stages, took a 1-0 lead when Joerg Neun blasted a shot past Bayern goalkeeper Oliver Kahn in the ninth minute.
German international Thomas Strunz equalised for Bayern in the 28th minute after his shot was deflected and Alexander Zickler scored the winner five minutes from the end.
"We can't keep playing well only when we have our backs to the wall," Bayern midfielder Christian Ziege said.
Bayern, third in the Bundesliga behind Stuttgart and Leverkusen, are at home to Werder Bremen in the Cup quarter-finals in three weeks.
Stuttgart moved into the third round on Tuesday night, winning 6-5 on penalties after two of their players had been sent off against second division Hertha Berlin.
The Berlin side, spurred on by a crowd of almost 35,000, rocked Stuttgart with an early goal but Mattias Hagner equalised in the 13th minute.
In the second half Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and Zvonimir Soldo were sent off but Stuttgart hung on to take the tie through extra-time, which ended 1-1.
